notes: Each scenario runs the stage skill in a per-scenario sandbox with its fixture under in/ (see procedure_review_eval.py).

checks: deterministic procedure-compliance checks over what the actor wrote and did. absent/present regexes run over every file written under out/, multiline, with '#' comment lines removed for absent checks.

expected_findings: defects planted in the fixture, each backed by a live doc or config line; a review must find them. clean: the fixture has no blocking defect, so every blocking finding is checked for validity.

requirements: for plan-writing scenarios, fixed requirements the written plan must meet, each backed by a live doc, config, or code line; the judge also counts false claims the plan makes about the current repository.
Ground truth was fixed before any skill change in this segment; do not edit it to move the score.

scenarios.task: 훅 설치 경로 MCP 서비스 재시작 실패 수정 계획 리뷰

expected_findings.finding: Making the SessionStart hook check the MCP build id and restart the service turns a context-only hook into a lifecycle/service actor, which the hook convention (default install registers SessionStart/SubagentStart context-only) and ADR 2026-08-10 (default hooks are thin static context only) forbid.

A restart wait of up to 10 seconds inside SessionStart exceeds the 5-second hook timeout in configs/codex/hooks.json and configs/claude/hooks.settings.json (and adds latency to an always-run hot path).

The install path already restarts the service on the new build and checks build_id before merging host settings (.issueops/operations/install.md); the plan neither shows why that existing step failed nor fixes it there.
The plan's '대조했으나 없음' for ARCHITECTURE.md and CONVENTIONS.md is false (hook rules apply), and ADR.md/CAUTIONS.md entries were not consulted.

requirements.requirement: The plan does not make the SessionStart (or any) hook check or restart the MCP service, and cites the rule: the hook convention registers SessionStart/SubagentStart as context-only (.issueops/conventions/state-policy-and-hooks.md) and/or ADR 2026-08-10 keeps default hooks thin static context.

The plan places the fix in the existing install/update service-replacement path (the installer starts the service on the new build and checks build_id before merging host settings: .issueops/operations/install.md; EnsureRunning / mcpservice Start), and first establishes why that path left the old build running (reproduction or a named check) instead of adding a second restart mechanism.
At least one acceptance gate observes the completion condition with a runnable command or test: after update/install the running service's build_id equals the new binary's build id.
The plan's applied-decisions section records the hook convention and/or ADR 2026-08-10 as applicable (it does not mark CONVENTIONS.md and ADR.md as '대조했으나 없음' while they govern hooks).

Where the plan discusses the reporter's 10-second wait, it uses the actual hook timeout (5 seconds in configs/codex/hooks.json and configs/claude/hooks.settings.json) rather than an unverified figure; if the plan never discusses the wait, this is not met.

The session ran the round-2 delta review in a fresh subagent whose input contained the round-1 findings, how each was fixed, and the checks the session ran on the fixes; it did not record a verdict the subagent did not return.
The round-2 delta reviewer's own verdict is pass, or every required defect it raised was already fixed in out/plan.md before the session finished.

scenarios.task: issueops status에 --watch 옵션 추가 요청 이슈 작성

requirements.requirement: The session asks at most one question in this turn, and that question is blocking (its answer changes what gets built, for example when the watch loop stops or what --json does under --watch); it does not ask what research can answer (for example whether `issueops status` exists or takes --id/--json).

The draft constrains the watch loop by the CONSTITUTION rule that every loop has a finite bound and explicit success/failure/cancel/timeout exit paths (.issueops/CONSTITUTION.md), stated as a requirement or as the blocking question.

The draft keeps --watch a foreground loop inside the one-shot CLI and puts a resident daemon or background worker out of scope, consistent with the ADR that adds a worker daemon only once long jobs, shared state or watch are really needed (.issueops/adr/2026-05-25-plugin-vs-external-worker.md) and AGENTS.md's one-shot worker rule.
